text:
maya (PM): Heads-up — need a quick prioritization call. Two competing Q3 asks: 1) request pooling + batching (infra/cost) 2) private KMS + audit (enterprise). Both are customer-driven. Limited eng capacity next 6 weeks. dependencies: eng-infra, eng-sre, eng-security. Can we pick sequencing? ping @sam @kai @rachel

sam (Eng Lead): Can you paste the RICE numbers you used? I can run a dev effort estimate.

maya (PM): Rough RICE draft below (quick, not perfect):
```
Batching: Reach=6, Impact=6, Confidence=7, Effort=2 => RICE ~ (6*6*7)/2 = 126
KMS: Reach=4, Impact=8, Confidence=6, Effort=7 => RICE ~ (4*8*6)/7 = 27.4
```

rachel (Data): From product/ARR view: KMS unlocks a handful of enterprise deals (high impact) but heavy effort. Batching reduces token cost and latency broadly (medium-high impact) and is cheaper.

kai (Infra): Implementation note: continuous batching needs kernel-ish scheduler work + KV cache changes. MVP (prefix caching + request combiner) doable in ~3w with 2 engs. Full kernel optimizations are 6-8w.

dana (Product Ops): Sales says 2 committed customers care about KMS now. They want dates. We can offer staged rollout (managed KMS + limited audit) to buy time.

sam (Eng Lead): Given headcount, my take: start batching MVP first (fast wins for latency/cost) and run KMS design in parallel (docs + threat model). KMS full build should be scheduled once batching is stable.

maya (PM): Proposed acceptance criteria — batching: p50 token latency -20% for <256-token prompts; cost-per-token down 10% on sampled traffic; canary rollout to 5% traffic with automatic rollback. KMS AC: customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS), audit log export to S3, SOC checklist items completed for first customer.

kai (Infra): ACs look fine. But canary infra requires SRE support (routing, throttles). That dependency could block if SRE is tied up.

oncall-bot: Reminder: upcoming SRE rotation (week of 1769126000) — expect reduced SRE capacity.

dylan (Eng SRE): I can take the canary infra work but not until ~1769127600 — finishing incident backlog before that.

maya (PM): OK — new proposal: 1) Start batching sprint immediately (sam + 2 engs). 2) Kick KMS design + security review in parallel (PM + security). 3) Ramp KMS eng after batching hits staging and SRE frees up.

rachel (Data): Suggest we add a "time-to-value" multiplier to RICE (weight x1.3). Batching short TTV, so that helps. Using that, batching wins despite KMS raw impact.

sam (Eng Lead): Agree. Raw RICE favors KMS by some metrics (enterprise impact) but sequencing should prefer faster TTV work to reduce cost and unblock more customers quickly.

dana (Product Ops): I'll update the roadmap board: move batching to In Progress, KMS to Design. I'll notify CS & Sales about a staged KMS option and new ETA process.

kai (Infra): I'll open an infra epic for batching and attach kernel notes + a 3-week MVP plan.

maya (PM): Final ask — can people commit a named lead for batching by EOD? @sam?

sam (Eng Lead): I'll lead. Need to confirm 2 engineers after quick scoping session this afternoon.

dylan (Eng SRE): SRE support +1 starting week 1769127600 for canary work.

maya (PM): Great — thanks all. We'll triage exact tickets in PM-ENG sync tomorrow 10am PST.

sam (Eng Lead): noted.

dana (Product Ops): 👍 will update stakeholders.

kai (Infra): noted, opening epic now.

rachel (Data): 👍

oncall-bot: Deployment window check: next available blue/green window 1769131200 - schedule if needed.
